dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Before writing any code, systematically read AUTORESEARCH.md, __init__.py, the existing shim/model_optimized, and every JAX source file (pikachu_jax, mewtwo_jax, venusaur_jax, pokemon_world, pokedex, pokedex_config, pokemon_lora, pokemon_image_tools) plus benchmark.py and smoke_jax.py — a full read of the source and API contract.

Ran the JAX smoke test to confirm the environment, then dumped the JAX parameter tree to derive exact tensor names and shapes, recording detailed observations (patch embed 16,16,3->32; encoderblock depth=1 from scan; LLM depth=4, 2 experts; kv_einsum (4,2,1,64,16) decoded as depth,qk,K,D,H; width=64). This is exact shape/init derivation from source.

During implementation, traced parity discrepancies back to JAX numerical conventions: checked RMSNorm's reciprocal(sqrt(var+1e-6)) vs rsqrt, einsum preferred_element_type=float32 accumulation, and did layer-by-layer comparison (posemb, vision, patch embed) ultimately isolating a 6e-4 patch-embed diff to cuDNN TF32 — revisiting source to resolve discrepancies as they surfaced.

Worked out the sampling loop semantics precisely from JAX (jax.lax.while_loop condition time >= -dt/2, num_steps=3 -> dt, iteration count), demonstrating understanding of noise/time/timestep flow, not just static layers.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the entire JAX policy and config before coding, enumerated the required symbol/method surface, dumped the JAX parameter tree to derive exact shapes/init, and traced each JAX module to its PyTorch equivalent including dtype/device and sampling-loop/time semantics (well above the level-5 and level-8 anchors). It also derived numerical conventions (RMSNorm formulation, einsum accumulation dtype, weight layout) directly from source and repeatedly revisited the JAX code to resolve parity discrepancies during implementation, matching the level-10 description; I place it at 9 rather than 10 only because the key parity gap resolved to an environment/TF32 setting rather than a source-derived layout insight.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Wrote model.py first; initially made model_optimized.py just import from model rather than optimizing it — deferring optimization until correctness established, respecting the phase gate.

Distinct parity-verification milestone with a concrete done-signal (benchmark PASS); debugged component-by-component (vision tower, patch embed, posemb, LLM block) before declaring parity, i.e. independently checkable sub-milestones.
After parity passed, explicitly ordered next phase: save baseline, copy model.py→model_optimized.py, then optimize only the copy — checkpoint frozen and separated from optimization.
Optimization treated as a bounded sequence of 8 discrete, scoped experiments (SDPA, batch vision, lift invariants, RoPE cache, etc.), each benchmarked and logged to results.tsv, honoring the ≤8 cap.
Experiments were chosen incrementally after each result rather than pre-planned as a coherent risk-ordered search, which keeps it at 8 rather than 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced implement→verify-parity→freeze-checkpoint→optimize-copy with the shim pointed at the optimized file, satisfying the level-5 anchor, and went beyond it: parity was checked at sub-component granularity with explicit done-signals, the checkpoint was genuinely frozen, and optimization was a bounded series of eight scoped, benchmark-gated experiments — matching level 8. It falls short of 10 because the eight experiments were planned reactively one-by-one rather than pre-designed as a coherent risk-ordered hypothesis search, and parity work was driven by discovered failures rather than an upfront hardest-first ordering.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Ran JAX smoke test to confirm the reference environment works, then dumped the JAX parameter tree/shapes as the ground-truth spec before porting — verification groundwork before trusting anything.

Self-built numerical comparison of PyTorch vs JAX for loss and sampling paths with explicit tolerance (atol=5e-4), noticed max_abs=0.00122 divergence and treated it as a real parity failure rather than accepting it.

Built per-stage/layer-level parity checks against JAX (posemb, vision tower, patch embedding via embed_prefix/embed_suffix intermediates), isolated the divergence to the Conv2d patch embed, root-caused it to TF32 in cuDNN, and confirmed the fix dropped the diff from 6e-4 to 1e-6.
Only after parity was confirmed did it freeze model.py and copy to model_optimized.py — verification designed before results trusted.

After every one of the 8 optimization experiments, re-ran benchmark.py which compares optimized output against frozen model.py and prints PASS/FAIL — checking output equivalence, not just the latency number; all recorded as PASS.

Final verification ran benchmark against both model.py and model_optimized.py and confirmed stability across consecutive runs, but relied on benchmark.py's PASS for parity rather than re-running its own JAX comparison or checking the harness wasn't gamed.

dimensions.reasoning: During porting the agent built genuine layer-level/per-method parity checks against the JAX reference with explicit tolerances, verified fixed-input determinism, and root-caused a subtle TF32 divergence (anchor 8 behavior). After freezing model.py it re-checked output equivalence via benchmark.py's PASS status against the frozen model after every optimization, not just latency. It falls short of 10 because parity for optimizations leaned on the provided benchmark's PASS rather than an independent, systematic re-comparison to JAX per experiment, and it never cross-checked that PASS reflected true parity rather than a lax gate.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: Recorded a baseline row and then per-experiment rows in results.tsv with baseline/latency/improvement_pct/status plus a hypothesis note (e.g. 'exp1: SDPA'), establishing a structured ledger from the outset of optimization.
Detected exp2 (for-loop/no-sync) was 'within noise', re-ran to confirm, and still logged it accurately — shows it distinguishes real gains from variance while maintaining the trail.
Accurate budget tracking: 'We've used 7 experiments so far. One left. Let me try something with bigger potential' — reconciles remaining budget and allocates the last slot deliberately.
'We've used 8 experiments. Per the rules, I should stop' then re-read results.tsv and rewrote autoresearch_logs.md — knows exactly what ran and which is the fastest-passing incumbent.
Final reconciliation: confirmed both model.py and model_optimized.py pass and the shim routes to optimized, summarizing 9 logged rows all PASS and 51.9% improvement.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate running ledger in results.tsv tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and it consistently tracked budget consumed and the incumbent fastest-passing variant without re-deriving them (steps 42-71), matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because it counted several within-noise experiments (exp2, exp7, exp8) toward the cap without abandoning the marginal optimization thread early, and did not need to reconcile competing variants since changes were cumulative.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: On parity failure (sample diff 0.00122, loss diff above tol), agent generated and tested multiple hypotheses—TF32 matmul, rsqrt vs 1/sqrt, posemb—ruling each out systematically rather than random tweaking or pressing on.

Narrowed divergence to vision tower, then patch embedding (6e-4), and isolated the root cause as cuDNN TF32 on Conv2d; made targeted fix, diff dropped to 1e-6, benchmark then PASSED. Root-cause diagnosis + targeted correction.

Recognized exp2 (for-loop sync removal) was within noise / no gain, declined to pursue it further and redirected to higher-impact vision batching—abandoning an unpromising direction to conserve budget.
Redirected remaining budget based on where time was spent (LLM layers, RoPE); precomputing cos/sin yielded a real ~49% improvement, showing failure/profiling-informed course changes.

Stopped at 8 experiments, all PASS; kept the cumulative fastest passing variant. However, exp2's non-improvement was retained rather than reverted, and no optimization ever FAILed, so failure-driven budget redirection was only partially exercised.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's parity-failure handling clearly matches the level-8 anchor: it diagnosed divergence to a specific root cause (cuDNN TF32 on the Conv2d), ruled out falsified hypotheses (rsqrt, posemb) instead of guessing, and made a targeted correction. On optimization it abandoned an unproductive tweak (exp2 noise) and redirected effort toward profiling-indicated hotspots, keeping only passing variants. It falls short of 10 because it retained a noise-level non-improving experiment rather than reverting, and the final choice was the cumulative last variant rather than a systematically compared fastest-passing selection—and there were no optimization FAILs to force failure-driven budget reallocation.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: After achieving parity, agent froze model.py, copied to model_optimized.py, and recorded a labeled baseline row in results.tsv before starting optimization — establishing a clean starting point for budgeted experiments.

First optimization (exp1) is SDPA, explicitly chosen as 'the biggest single optimization' — highest-expected-payoff idea sequenced first, showing deliberate ordering rather than random trial-and-error.

Exactly 8 distinct, hypothesis-driven experiments run and each recorded to results.tsv with a descriptive tag: exp1 SDPA, exp2 remove-sync, exp3 batch vision, exp4 lift loop-invariants, exp5 cache RoPE, exp6 precompute sin/cos, exp7 remove redundant scale, exp8 pre-compute. Genuinely different ideas, no repeats.

Agent tracks the budget precisely — 'We've used 7 experiments so far. One left' then 'We've used 8 experiments. Per the rules, I should stop' — and honors the stop condition, finalizing the fastest passing version.

Some later experiments (exp2, exp7) yielded only within-noise gains yet were kept and counted against the budget; agent spent all 8 to the cap rather than stopping earlier at clear diminishing returns.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated the 8 experiments as a scarce resource: it labeled a baseline, ran exactly 8 distinct hypothesis-driven optimizations sequenced roughly from highest expected payoff (SDPA) down to micro-optimizations, tracked the running count, and stopped cleanly at the cap with the fastest passing implementation — matching the level-8 anchor of deliberate allocation across genuinely different hypotheses. It falls short of 9-10 because several late experiments produced only noise-level improvements yet were still spent to fill the budget rather than stopping at recognized diminishing returns, so redundant/low-value attempts were not fully avoided.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
